section_summary: Pages 225–238 conclude Research Report No. 76, Part III, an Allied analysis of Japanese military psychology, ceremonial dates, Bushido, State Shinto, revenge, and wartime indoctrination, followed by three historical and cultural appendices. Pages 239–243 contain a confidential 1941 Committee on East Asia circular reviewing five Japanese militarist books that advocate total mobilization, the Axis-aligned “New Order,” the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, and preparation for war with the United States. Page 244 is a 1940 State Department memorandum about Japanese propaganda intended for overseas Chinese communities.

subfiles.title: Research Report No. 76, Part III — Ceremonial Days, Conclusions, and Appendices A–C
subfiles.about: The concluding portion of an Allied intelligence study analyzes Japanese ceremonial dates, military psychology, Bushido, State Shinto, revenge, and the cultural foundations of wartime behavior.
subfiles.summary: The report argues that Japanese leaders deliberately exploited imperial and military anniversaries to increase fighting spirit, schedule operations, and anticipate Allied actions on holidays or recurrent dates. Its conclusions portray Japanese military conduct as the product of modern indoctrination built around Bushido, emperor worship, racial superiority, permanent offensive action, contempt for surrender, and revenge. Three appendices reproduce Chamberlain’s critique of modern Japanese militarism and imperial ideology, an account of the conflict between duty and humanity in Japanese drama, and Colonel Harold Doud’s description of a strenuous Japanese regimental holiday.

subfiles.title: CEA 85 — Strictly Confidential Reviews of Current Japanese Books
subfiles.doc_type: confidential circular letter with book-review enclosure
subfiles.from: John H. Reisner, Secretary, Committee on East Asia
subfiles.to: Secretaries of Mission Boards having work in East Asia
subfiles.about: A confidential missionary circular distributes reviews of five contemporary Japanese books expressing militarist, totalitarian, expansionist, and anti-American ideas.
subfiles.summary: The circular identifies recurring claims that Germany would win the war, democracy and liberalism were obsolete, and Japan’s Axis-aligned program possessed a uniquely spiritual or divine mission. Reviews of works by Kurazo Suzuki, Kazuo Higo, Gunpei Sekine, Nobumasa Suetsugu, and Chuko Ikezaki discuss the total defense state, emperor-centered historical ideology, the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, suppression of China, and anticipated naval war with the United States. The authors envision Japanese leadership over China, Manchukuo, Southeast Asia, India, Australia, and the Pacific while dismissing or attacking Christianity and Western political values.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Propaganda to Overseas Chinese
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE: Ballantine; HJN)
subfiles.about: The memorandum summarizes intercepted Japanese communications concerning the preparation and overseas distribution of propaganda aimed at Chinese communities.
subfiles.summary: British-censored messages intercepted at Hong Kong indicated coordinated propaganda activity by Japanese military authorities and consular officials in China, Southeast Asia, and the Americas. The material included pamphlets and phonograph records for overseas Chinese audiences; the Japanese consul general at Batavia reportedly advised avoiding attacks on Chiang Kai-shek because they irritated overseas Chinese.
